rows.question: Where do I report an absence?
rows.answer:
To report a student absence at Vista Ridge High School, you have a few options:

- You can submit absence notes or medical documentation by email from the parent/guardian's email address on file to VRHSattendance@leanderisd.org.
- You can hand deliver absence notes or medical documentation to the Attendance Office.
- Absence notes should be received within two days after the student returns to school.
- Notes are welcome in English and Spanish.

For more details, you can also refer to the [Absence for students](https://www.leanderisd.org/attendance) page.

If you need to report an early dismissal, parents can email VRHSearlydismissal@leanderisd.org (before 10:30AM) to request a student to leave early.

Let me know if you need help with anything else!

rows.question: What is the student check-out policy?
rows.answer:
Here is the student check-out policy at Vista Ridge High School for the 2026-2027 school year:

- **Parent/Guardian Presence Required:** To check a student out early, a parent or guardian must come to the front office in person, provide a photo ID, and check the student out.  
- **No Phone Calls Accepted:** For student safety, phone calls requesting early release are not accepted.
- **Advance Notice:** Please arrive at least 20 minutes before you need your student to be released, due to the high volume of requests.
- **No Early Check-Outs After 2:45 pm:** In-person early check-outs are not allowed after 2:45 pm. After this time, students must wait for regular dismissal.
- **Student Sign-In/Out:** Students must sign in and out at the Attendance Window when leaving or returning to campus.
- **Documentation Required:** After your student’s absence, you must provide a note or email documenting the reason for the absence. This should include the student’s full legal name, ID number, grade, exact dismissal time, and reason for dismissal. Emails sent before 10:30 AM can be used for check-outs later in the day.
- **Excused Absences:** Proper documentation helps keep your student out of truancy proceedings and may be important for attendance appeals.

For full details and step-by-step instructions, visit: [How To Check Your Student Out Early](https://sites.google.com/leanderisd.org/vrhsattendance/student-sign-out).

If you have any other questions, feel free to ask!
sources: How To Check Your Student Out Early

rows.question: How do I appeal an attendance decision?
rows.answer:
To appeal an attendance decision at Vista Ridge High School—specifically if you owe hours due to falling below 90% attendance in a course—you will need to follow the school's attendance appeal process. Here’s what the context says:

- Appeals can only be made for extenuating circumstances (such as medical procedures or emergencies).
- You will need to provide supporting documentation for your appeal. Without documentation, the appeal will be denied.
- The appeal is reviewed by the school's hours owed appeals committee.

**Steps to start an appeal:**
1. Contact your Assistant Principal to discuss your situation and request an Attendance Appeal Request Form.
2. Complete the form, attach any supporting documentation, and submit it as directed by your Assistant Principal.

If you have questions or need to begin the process, you should reach out to your Assistant Principal. You can find their contact information on the [Assistant Principals' Office page](https://sites.google.com/leanderisd.org/vrhs-assistant-principals-offi/home).

If you need further assistance and are not sure who your Assistant Principal is, you can also call the front office at 512-570-1800.

Let me know if you need help finding the right contact or have any other questions!

rows.question: How do I register for AP tests?
rows.answer:
To register for AP tests at Vista Ridge High School for the 2026-2027 school year, you need to complete two main steps:

### 1. Register and Pay in Total Registration
- Go to the [Total Registration Link](https://user.totalregistration.net/AP/441176).
- Create an account (or log in if you already have one).
- Select your exams and pay the fee online ($85 per exam, or $27 per exam if you qualify for free/reduced lunch).
- Registration and payment are due by **October 28, 2026**. After this date, a $40 late fee per exam applies.

### 2. Join Your AP Class in College Board AP Classroom
- Go to [myap.collegeboard.org](https://myap.collegeboard.org/login).
- Log in or create a College Board account.
- Use the join code provided by your AP teacher to enroll in each AP class section.
- Indicate whether you plan to take the AP exam (“YES” or “NO”) in AP Classroom. The default is “YES,” so change it if you do not plan to test.

**Both steps must be completed for your registration to be valid.**

#### Additional Notes:
- If you need help or want to cancel an exam, contact the campus Dean of Instruction, Olga Angelo-Day, at olga.angelo-day@leanderisd.org.
- For students taking second semester AP Government or Macroeconomics, registration is open January 5 – February 18, 2027.
- If you need accommodations, requests must be submitted through SSD Online by January 22, 2027.
- For free/reduced lunch fee eligibility, apply on the [Leander ISD Child Nutrition Services page](https://www.leanderisd.org/childnutritionservices/#frlunch).

You can find more details and step-by-step instructions on the [AP Test Registration Info](https://vrhs.leanderisd.org/ap-test-registration) page.

Good luck with your AP exams, Ranger! If you have any questions, feel free to ask.

rows.question: What do seniors need to do before graduation?
rows.answer:
Here are the main things Vista Ridge High School seniors (Class of 2027) need to do before graduation, based on the current information available:

- **Complete the FAFSA:** Filling out the FAFSA is a graduation requirement. The FAFSA opens October 1st, and the priority deadline for most Texas universities is January 15th. Check each university for their specific deadlines.
- **Order Cap and Gown:** The only required item for graduation is the Cap, Gown & Tassel Unit, which you order through Herff Jones. More information and order packets are provided during the senior meeting in October.
- **Clear All Obligations and Hours:** All school obligations and owed hours must be cleared before you can pick up your cap and gown.
- **Attend Graduation Practice:** Participation in graduation practice is required. Immediately after, there is a "Clap Out" event.
- **Senior Activities:** Participate in events like the Senior Panoramic Picture, Senior Awards (invitation only), Senior SAIL, and Project Graduation.
- **Elementary Graduation Walks:** Seniors can return to their LISD elementary school in cap and gown for a traditional walk. Transportation is not provided.
- **Google Account Transition:** After graduation (usually around July), your school Google account will transition to an alumni account, which remains active for one year. Download any files you want to keep to your personal computer.
- **Follow Cap Decorating Guidelines:** If you decorate your cap, follow the school’s guidelines to ensure it is appropriate for the ceremony.

For more details or updates, check the [Seniors 2027 page](https://vrhs.leanderisd.org/seniors-2027) and the [Project Graduation page](https://sites.google.com/view/vistaridgeprojectgrad/home).

If you have specific questions about your requirements, your counselor is the best person to ask. Good luck with your senior year, Ranger!

You can contact the Vista Ridge High School Counseling Office in the following ways:

- Email Kristen Schneider at kristen.schneider@leanderisd.org.
- Visit the [Counseling Services website](https://sites.google.com/leanderisd.org/vrhs-counseling-services/home) for more information.

rows.question: What is Ranger Time?
rows.answer:
Ranger Time at Vista Ridge High School is a flexible period built into the school schedule. It is sometimes referred to as "Minga-Flextime" because it is managed through the Minga platform. During Ranger Time, students have the opportunity to participate in various activities, such as:

- Attending club meetings (for example, Rangers Alliance and Crafting for Kindness both meet during Ranger Time)
- Participating in workshops, volunteer drives, or personal growth activities
- Receiving academic support or enrichment

Ranger Time is designed to help students build friendships, develop leadership skills, and engage in both on-campus and community activities. You can access the Ranger Time Portal here: [Ranger Time Portal](https://adv.leanderisd.org/login.aspx?ReturnUrl=%2fDefault.aspx).

If you have more specific questions about how Ranger Time works or how to sign up for activities, feel free to ask!

rows.question: What time does the school day end?
rows.answer:
The regular school day at Vista Ridge High School ends at 3:35 p.m. 

If you need the schedule for a late start or early release day, let me know and I can provide those times as well! Go Rangers!

rows.question: How do I report bullying?
rows.answer:
You can report bullying at Vista Ridge High School by visiting the [Bullying Prevention](https://www.leanderisd.org/bullying) page. This page provides information and resources for reporting and addressing bullying concerns within Leander ISD.

If you need further assistance or have specific concerns, you can also contact the front office at 512-570-1800, and they can direct you to the appropriate staff member.

If you have any more questions or need support, please let me know!

rows.question: How do I access my STAAR scores?
rows.answer:
You can access your STAAR scores in two main ways:

### 1. Through the Home Access Center (HAC)
- Log into your LISD Home Access Center (HAC): [Home Access Center](https://www.leanderisd.org/homeaccess)
- At the top of the Home Access screen, click on the "Grades" icon.
- Next to "Report Card" on the left-hand side, click on "Texas Test Scores."
- Your STAAR results will appear, or you’ll be directed to click to go to the Texas Student Portal.

### 2. Through the Texas Assessment Parent Portal
- Go to [texasassessment.gov](https://www.texasassessment.gov).
- Click "Log In to Parent Portal."
- Enter your child’s Unique Access Code and date of birth.
    - If you don’t know the access code, click "How do I find my access code?" and enter your child’s legal first name and TSDS ID (usually their social security number) to retrieve it.
- View your performance level and download the full Confidential Student Report (CSR).

### Need Help?
If you have trouble accessing the portal or have questions about your results, you can contact:
- Principal: Keith Morgan | 512-570-1810 | keith.morgan@leanderisd.org
- Campus Testing Coordinator: Linsey Cernero | 512-570-1823 | linsey.cernero@leanderisd.org

Let me know if you need instructions in Spanish or have any other questions!
